## Conservative cost estimates (AWS & OpenAI)

**Question: Do you think we can have a rough estimate of cloud costs for each hour of live operation?**

*Generated by: GPT-5.6-Sol (medium)*

A reasonable estimate is about $0.053–$0.056 per live hour for light manual use, excluding OpenAI inference. I would budget $0.06/hour to leave some margin.

That is approximately:

- $0.45 for an 8-hour session
- $1.35 per day
- $40 per month if accidentally left running continuously

Prices checked for us-east-1 on 2026-11-12, without assuming free-tier credits or discounts.

## Estimated hourly AWS cost

| Component | Approx. hourly cost | Basis |
|---|---:|---|
| Internal Application Load Balancer | $0.02250 | Fixed ALB hourly charge |
| One 0.5-vCPU, 1-GB Fargate task | $0.02469 | $0.02024 CPU + $0.00445 memory |
| Task public IPv4 address | $0.00500 | One address while the task runs |
| Secrets Manager | $0.00056 | One secret prorated from $0.40/month |
| ECR image storage | ~$0.00014 | Assumes one 1-GB image |
| ALB traffic/LCU | ~$0.0001–$0.001 | Very light interactive traffic |
| CloudFront | ~$0–$0.002 | Requests and bytes transferred |
| CloudWatch Logs | ~$0–$0.001 | Sparse logs, no access logging |
| Cognito | $0 | One test user is inside the MAU free tier |
| S3 Terraform state | Effectively $0 | Tiny objects and very few requests |
| VPC, subnets, routes, IAM, ECS cluster | $0 | No direct hourly charge |
| Expected total | $0.053–$0.056/hour | Light manual testing |

AWS’s published rates support the main components:

- Fargate Linux/x86 in us-east-1 is billed per vCPU-second and GB-second. Our task works out to about $0.02469/hour. AWS Fargate pricing
- An ALB costs $0.0225/hour, plus consumed LCUs. Elastic Load Balancing pricing
- An in-use public IPv4 address costs $0.005/hour. Amazon VPC pricing
- One secret costs $0.40/month, or approximately $0.00056/hour. Secrets Manager pricing
- ECR private-image storage is $0.10/GB-month. Amazon ECR pricing

## Why the ALB dominates

Our Fargate task can be stopped, but an ALB has a fixed hourly charge as long as it exists.

That gives us two materially different states:

| Deployment state | Approx. AWS cost |
|---|---:|
| Terraform applied, ECS desired count 0 | ~$0.023/hour |
| One ECS task running | ~$0.053–$0.056/hour |
| Application stack destroyed; bootstrap retained | Pennies per month or less |

With the service stopped, we avoid:

- Fargate CPU and memory charges.
- The task’s public IPv4 charge.
- Runtime log and request costs.

But we still pay for:

- The ALB.
- Secrets Manager.
- ECR image storage.
- Tiny amounts of state storage.

Therefore, setting desired_count = 0 is useful for short pauses, but it is not equivalent to teardown.

## Request-dependent costs

For one developer performing a smoke test, traffic charges should remain tiny.

For example, suppose one hour produces:

- 1,000 CloudFront HTTPS requests.
- 10 MB of application traffic.
- 1 MB of logs.

A rough additional cost would be:

- CloudFront requests: about $0.001.
- CloudFront transfer: under $0.001.
- ALB LCU processing: around $0.0001.
- CloudWatch log ingestion: around $0.0005 before any applicable allowance.

CloudFront VPC origins have no separate surcharge, and transfer from the AWS origin to CloudFront is waived. AWS CloudFront VPC-origin guidance

Cognito should cost nothing for our handful of Google test users; social-provider users have a 10,000-MAU monthly free tier. Amazon Cognito pricing

## OpenAI cost is separate

OpenAI inference is not included in the AWS estimate.

Our selected snapshot, gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17, currently costs:

- $0.75 per million input tokens.
- $0.075 per million cached input tokens.
- $4.50 per million output tokens.

Those are the current values in the official OpenAI documentation.

Our two measured Slice 1.1 questions cost:

- Answered question: $0.00168
- Insufficient-evidence question: $0.00238
- Average: approximately $0.002/question

For budgeting, I would allow up to $0.03 per submitted question, even though our observed cases were much cheaper. This accounts for longer outputs and all three permitted model turns.

The AWS $10 budget alert does not cover OpenAI charges; those belong to the separate OpenAI account.

## Practical budget interpretation

At a conservative $0.06 per running hour:

$10 / $0.06 ≈ 166 hours

So the account-level budget could theoretically cover about seven continuous days of this stack, assuming no unrelated AWS spending. We should not treat that as permission to leave it running, because:

- The alert is not a hard spending limit.
- The account may have other costs.
- Billing data and alerts can be delayed.
- Partial ALB hours are billed as full hours.
- Failed deployment attempts can temporarily run overlapping Fargate tasks.

For the planned deployment experiment, a more useful working allowance is:

8 live hours × $0.06 ≈ $0.48 AWS infrastructure

Even allowing for provisioning, rollback, repeated task replacements, logs, traffic, and price-estimation error, $1 of AWS allowance should comfortably cover a focused one-day experiment. The $10 alert leaves substantial safety margin, provided we complete teardown afterward.
